title: A string toolkit
description:
Build a little text-processing tool. Every line of input is a command followed by its text, and the program prints one line of result for each:

```
upper Hello, World
reverse stressed
words  the quick   brown fox
replace a o banana
caesar 3 Hello, xyz!
palindrome A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
palindrome pointer
shout hello
```

prints

```
HELLO, WORLD
desserts
4 words
bonono
Khoor, abc!
yes
no
Unknown command: shout
```

| Command | Prints |
|---|---|
| `upper TEXT` / `lower TEXT` | the text in upper or lower case |
| `reverse TEXT` | the text backwards |
| `words TEXT` | how many words: `N words`, or `1 word` |
| `replace X Y TEXT` | the text with every character X changed to Y (X and Y are single characters) |
| `caesar N TEXT` | letters shifted N places along the alphabet (N from 0 to 25), wrapping from z to a and keeping their case; other characters unchanged |
| `palindrome TEXT` | `yes` if the letters and digits read the same both ways, ignoring case, otherwise `no` |

The text is everything after the single space that follows the command (and its arguments). Empty lines are skipped. A command whose arguments cannot be read (`replace ab`, `caesar x hello`, `caesar 30 hi`) prints `Could not read: ` and the line. Lines are at most 500 characters.
requirements: Each command is its own function that takes a `char *` (or `const char *`) and works on the text in place or by walking it with pointers.
`reverse` swaps characters from both ends with two pointers moving towards each other.
The commands are chosen by comparing the first word with `strcmp`.

shout hello

examples.name: edge cases
examples.stdin:
lower MiXeD 123
reverse a
reverse
words one
words
caesar 0 same
caesar 25 Abc
caesar 13 Hello

palindrome
palindrome 12321
examples.expected:
mixed 123
a

1 word
0 words
same
Zab
Uryyb
yes
yes
